area: Headquarters "hire / manage a manager" UI presentation (HR/Pricing/Logistics/Purchasing/Headhunter manager plans)
findings:
WHERE THE PLAYER CLICKS — it is a HQ BUILDING PANEL INSIDE THE SMARTPHONE "BizMan" APP, not a standalone app and not the Headhunter building.

Path: Smartphone -> open the BizMan app (AppName.BizMan, class UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.BizMan in .../decomp/BigAmbitions/UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan/BizMan.cs). BizMan.OnEnable shows BizManList (BizManList.cs). BizManList holds a HeadquartersList (UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan/HeadquartersList.cs) that renders one row per player building where `x.RentedByPlayer && x.businessTypeName == "ba:businesstype_headquarters"`. Each HQ row has a logo, address, SetDestination button, and an "EmployeeCounter" strip of 5 buttons named exactly: PricingManagers, LogisticsManagers, PurchasingAgents, HRManagers, Headhunters — each showing the count of employees with that skill at that address (EmployeeHelper.GetEmployeeInstances with withAssignedAddress+withSkills). Clicking the row or any counter calls `InstanceBehavior<UIs>.Instance.fullMenu.bizMan.Open(headquarters.Address, tabName)`.

BizMan.Open -> business.SetAddress + business.SetInitialTab(tab) + business.Open(). BizManBusiness (top-level file decomp/BigAmbitions/BizManBusiness.cs) is the per-building panel. BizManBusiness.SetUpTabs() builds the tab strip from a hardcoded if/else on businessTypeName; for "ba:businesstype_headquarters" (and only if buildingRegistration.RentedByPlayer) the tabs are: Presentation, Schedule, PricingManagers, LogisticsManagers, PurchasingAgents, HRManagers, Headhunters, Settings. Tab button names live as `public const string` on BizMan (HrManagersTab="HRManagers", etc.). SetTab(name) does `containers.Find(name).gameObject.SetActive(true)` — the tab bodies are pre-authored child GameObjects of a `containers` transform on the BizManBusiness prefab, and activating one fires that component's OnEnable().

"HIRE" IS NOT DONE IN THESE TABS. The HQ tabs only create "plans" and bind an ALREADY-HIRED employee to a plan via a dropdown. There is no Hire button anywhere in the HQ panel. Getting a manager is the ordinary employee pipeline:
1. Recruit a candidate with a manager skill: ba:skill_hrmanager / ba:skill_pricingmanager / ba:skill_logisticsmanager / ba:skill_purchasingagent / ba:skill_headhunter. Entry points: (a) a Recruitment Agency building/phone dialog — Dialogs/RecruitmentAgencyDialog.cs -> creates Entities.RecruitmentCampaign; requires DiplomaName.BasicHr completed and at least one named player business. (b) The in-game "Headhunters" feature — BizMan -> HQ -> Headhunters tab -> HeadhuntersRecruitingTab.cs: skillNameDropdown (all SkillHelper.AllSkillNames minus HeadhunterHelper.skillsToSkipWhenRecruiting), skill-target slider, deal-breakers, StartRecruiting -> plan.StartRecruiting(); recruits land as candidates. (c) Job board.
   Candidate creation: Helpers/RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate(skillName, skillValue, address, ...) — a switch news a typed subclass: "ba:skill_hrmanager" => new HRManager(), pricingmanager => new PricingManager(), logisticsmanager => new LogisticsManager(), headhunter => new Headhunter(), default => new EmployeeInstance(). It adds to SaveGameManager.Current.CandidateEmployeeInstances and fires GameEvent "ba:gameevent_candidatereceived".
2. Smartphone -> My Employees app (AppName.MyEmployees, UI.Smartphone.Apps.MyEmployees/MyEmployees.cs) -> "Candidates" tab (candidatesTabButton; CandidateScrollerController -> CandidateCellView rows). CandidateCellView.Hire() -> EmployeeHelper.HireCandidate(instance): removes from CandidateEmployeeInstances, adds to EmployeeInstancesDictionary + GetEmployeeInstances(), sets dayHired, fires "ba:gameevent_employeehired". Now identical to any hired employee (appears in the "Employees" tab, paid wages via EmployeeHelper.PayDailyWages). CandidateCellView also has Negotiate() and an assignBusiness dropdown.
3. Assign the hired manager's home address to the HQ: employee.assignedAddress = hqAddress (CandidateCellView.AssignBusiness / EmployeeCellView / MyEmployees employee panel dropdown).
4. Schedule the manager into a WorkShift at the HQ: BizMan -> HQ -> Schedule tab (ScheduleDay.workShifts / WorkShift). This is required — see next.
5. Only now does the manager appear in the HQ plan's "assign manager" dropdown. Every plan list filters with the same predicate, e.g. HrManagersPlanList.UpdateHrManagerDropdownForPlan: `x.assignedAddress == bizMan.business.address && x.HasSkill("ba:skill_hrmanager") && !anyOtherPlanOfThisType.assignedEmployeeId==x.id && x.IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift()`.

FULL UI CLASS LIST — HR Managers feature (namespace UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.HRManagers, folder .../UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.HrManagers/):
- HrManagersPlanList (HrManagersPlanList.cs): the tab-body component. OnEnable() -> RefreshManagersList(): iterates HrManagerHelper.GetAssignedPlansForHeadquarters(bizMan.business.address), instantiates one `entryTemplate` row per plan, plus a `buttonEntry` "+ add plan" row, wraps them in a ReorderableList (drag reorders SaveGameManager.Current.hrManagerPlans). Row shows manager name or "common_unassigned" + an inline ManagerDropdown (shown when the row is selected) + "N/Max" Info label + health-insurance icon. AddPlan() -> new HrManagerPlan{ headquartersAddress = bizMan.business.address } added to SaveGameManager.Current.hrManagerPlans, then SelectPlan. SelectPlan -> UpdateHrManagerDropdownForPlan + hrManagerPlanUI.LoadPlan(plan) + wires noManagerAssignedPopUp.onChooseEmployee. OnChangedHrManager/ChangeHrManager -> plan.AssignEmployee(id) (sets HrManagerPlan.assignedEmployeeId) with HudConfirm dialogs if the new manager's skill can't cover current assigned employees / health insurance.
- HrManagerPlanUI (HrManagerPlanUI.cs): the right-hand detail panel. LoadPlan(HrManagerPlan) drives it (no OnEnable — list-driven). Controls: replaceAbsentEmployeesToggle, trainingTargetSlider (+trainingTargetValue %), averageSalary/averageSatisfaction/averagePrimarySkill bars, employeesScrollerController (assigned workers), assignEmployeesList + assignableEmployeesScrollerController (OpenAssignEmployeesList), Fill()/ClearAssignedEmployees() bulk buttons, health-insurance cancel/upgrade buttons. SetEmployeeAssigned(employeeId, assigned) -> plan.assignedEmployees.Add/Remove + EmployeeHelper.GetEmployeeById(id).assignedHrManagerPlanId = plan.id/null; fires onAssignedEmployeesChanged. Holds a public NoManagerAssignedPopUp noManagerAssignedPopUp.
- EmployeesScrollerController (EmployeesScrollerController.cs): `BaTable<EmployeeCellView, HrManagerEmployeeModel>`; Load(list, includeUnassignedEmployees, managerId) builds rows; used for both assigned list and assign list.
- EmployeeCellView (UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.HrManagers/EmployeeCellView.cs): a row.
- HrManagerEmployeeModel : BaseEmployeeModel (HrManagerEmployeeModel.cs): row model (businessName, insuranceDemand, assigned).
- HeadhunterEmployeeCellView / HeadhunterEmployeeModel / HeadhunterEmployeesScrollerController (same folder): rows for headhunter recruits / no-manager popup lists.
- NoManagerAssignedPopUp (top-level decomp/BigAmbitions/NoManagerAssignedPopUp.cs, global namespace): SHARED by all 5 plan types. Show(blockDeleteButton=false) sets planCanvasGroup.alpha=0.5, interactable=false, and shows employeeDropdown. SetUpEmployeeDropdown(List<EmployeeInstance>) fills it with "common_unassigned" + names. Awake wires employeeDropdown.onOptionSelected -> onChooseEmployee(index-1). Also exposes deletePlan / onDeletePlan Actions and DeletePlan() -> HudConfirm "bizman_delete_plan_confirm".
- Non-UI model/helpers: Buildings.Office.Headquarters.HrManagerPlan (id, assignedEmployeeId, headquartersAddress, assignedEmployees List<string>, replaceAbsentEmployees, trainingTarget, healthInsurancePlan; MaxEmployees => HrManagerSkillValue.CalculateMaxAssignableEmployees() = 10 + floor(skill/25)*10; AssignEmployee/UnAssignEmployee/Delete; TrainEmployees()/PayHealthInsurance() run daily) and HrManagerHelper (GetPlanFromId, GetAssignedPlanForHrManager, GetAssignedPlansForHeadquarters(Address), DeletePlan, CalculateMaxAssignableEmployees extension).

PARALLEL CLASS SETS (same "plan list + plan detail + NoManagerAssignedPopUp + Buildings.Office.Headquarters helper/plan" shape):
- Pricing: UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.PricingManagers.{PricingManagersPlanList, PricingManagersPlanListEntry, PricingManagerPlanUI, PricingManagerProductsScrollerController, PricingManagerProductCellView, PricingManagerProductModel, PricingManagerFilterController, PricingManagerFilterToggle} + Buildings.Office.Headquarters.{PricingManagerPlan, PricingManagerHelper, PricingManagerSettings, PriceSuggestion, OriginalStorePrice}. Plan config = pick a supervisedNeighborhood (plan.SetSupervisedNeighborhood); GetSupervisedStores() = all PricingManagerHelper.IsManageableBusiness in that neighborhood; RunUpdate()/IsUpdateDue(); notifies via Notifications.Show("notifications_PricingManager_mispriced_items", onClick -> bizMan.Open(hq,"PricingManagers") + pricingManagersPlanList.SelectPlanById).
- Logistics: UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.LogisticsManagers.{LogisticsManagersPlanList, LogisticsManagersPlanListEntry, LogisticsManagerPlanUI, LogisticsManagerDestinationUI, LogisticsManagerListSortable, LogisticsManagerListOption, LogisticsManagerListEntryData} + Buildings.Office.Headquarters.{LogisticsManagerPlan, LogisticsManagerHelper} + LogisticsManagerPlanDestination. Plan config = pick a warehouse (warehouseDropdown) + add up to MaxDestinations destination stores, each with a per-product min-stock ("min_stock_amount") / factory "deliver up to" target, +/- steppers, "runs out in N days" readout. Runtime: LogisticsManagerHelper.DoAllWarehouseDeliveries()/DoAllFactoryDeliveries() iterate SaveGameManager.Current.logisticsManagerPlans, enqueue plan.GetPlannedDeliveries() into DistributedWork; LogisticsManagerPlan.DeliverDestination restocks from the player Warehouse and, on failure, sends phone messages through Contact.EnsurePermanentContact("logistics_alerts", ContactCategoryName.ImportsAndGoods, ...).SendMessage(new TextMessage("ba:messagetype_phone_logistics_manager_delivery_no_stock"/"...no_available_space")) + Notifications.Show(Warning,"delivery_alert_notification"...). THIS is the closest existing analog to the user's target #5/#6/#7, but it delivers from a player-owned Warehouse rather than editing the store's DeliveryContract.
- Purchasing agents: UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.PurchasingAgentsPlanList (in the BizMan folder, not a sub-namespace) + UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.PurchasingAgent.PurchasingAgentPlanUI + Buildings.Office.Headquarters.PurchasingAgentHelper. Here the "plan" object is Entities.ImportPartnership (has employeeInstanceId, importAddress, nextDeliveryDay; dropdown interactability gated by DeliveryHelper.CanModifyContract(plan.nextDeliveryDay)).
- Headhunters: UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.Headhunters.HeadhuntersPlanList + HeadhunterPlanUI (top-level file, global ns) + HeadhuntersRecruitingTab + HeadhuntersAutomaticReplacementTab + HeadhuntersDealBreakers + Buildings.Office.Headquarters.{HeadhunterPlan, HeadhunterHelper}. HeadhunterPlan.assignedHrPlans (string[]) — a headhunter supervises HR-manager plans, not stores.

HOW THE UIs ARE REGISTERED (what a mod could imitate/hook):
- Smartphone apps: FullMenu (UI.Smartphone/FullMenu.cs) has `[SerializeField] SmartphoneApps apps` (Player.HUD.SmartphoneUI.SmartphoneApps : ScriptableObject { SmartphoneApp[] appList }). FullMenu.Start() iterates `apps.appList.Where(x => x.showInFullMenu)` to build app buttons; the app bodies are pre-authored children of FullMenu.appsContainer matched by name == AppName.ToStringFast(). FullMenu.SelectApp(AppName) simply activates the matching child. AppName (decomp/BigAmbitions/AppName.cs) is a plain 8-value enum {Persona,Contacts,MyEmployees,BizMan,EconoView,VoogleMaps,MarketInsider,Rivals} — NOT [Flags], not data-driven. No registry/factory/event to add an app.
- BizMan tabs: BizManBusiness holds serialized references to every tab component (hrManagersPlanList, hrHrManagerPlanUI, pricingManagersPlanList, logisticsLogisticsManagersPlanList, purchasingAgentsPlanList, bizManSchedule, bizManInsight, ...). Tab visibility is a hardcoded if/else in SetUpTabs(); tab bodies are name-matched children of `containers`; SetTab activates by name -> OnEnable. No registry/event; the only extension seam is Harmony on BizManBusiness.SetUpTabs / SetTab plus instantiating your own GameObject under `containers`.
- Manager runtime: managers run through EmployeeInstance polymorphism. Entities.HRManager : EmployeeInstance overrides WorkDaily() -> HrManagerHelper.GetAssignedPlanForHrManager(id).TrainEmployees()+PayHealthInsurance(); EmployeeHelper.WorkDaily() loops all employees calling virtual WorkDaily(). The subclass is chosen only in RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate's switch, and persisted by save-system polymorphism (see CompatibilityFixesEA04.FixHRManagerNotHavingCorrectClass). Plans live in flat lists on GameInstance: SaveGameManager.Current.hrManagerPlans / pricingManagerPlans / logisticsManagerPlans / headhunterPlans / importPartnerships. Events available: GlobalEvents.onNewDay/onNewHour/onSaveGame, GameEvent.Invoke("ba:gameevent_employeehired"/"ba:gameevent_candidatereceived"/"ba:gameevent_startedrecruitmentcampaign").

HQ EXISTENCE GATE:
- HeadquartersList.Load() only lists BuildingRegistrations where RentedByPlayer && businessTypeName == "ba:businesstype_headquarters". No such registration => no HQ row => no entry to the manager tabs at all.
- BizManBusiness.SetUpTabs() adds the 5 manager tabs only when buildingRegistration.RentedByPlayer && businessTypeName == "ba:businesstype_headquarters".
- To create a Headquarters: rent a building whose BuildingType equals the Headquarters BusinessType's suitableBuildingType (an office building), then BizMan -> Settings tab (BizManSettings.cs): businessTypeDropdown is filtered to `BusinessTypeHelper.GetAllPlayerAvailableBusinesses().Where(x => x.suitableBuildingType == building.BuildingType)`; pick "Headquarters", give it a non-empty name, Save -> ChangeBusinessType -> adds HappinessHelper modifier "ba:happinessmodifier_started_a_headquarters". So the gate = own/rent an office building + establish it as the Headquarters business type. (Recruiting managers additionally needs DiplomaName.BasicHr for the Recruitment Agency.)

SCREENSHOT-LEVEL FLOW — GET A MANAGER HIRED:
Rent office building -> BizMan app -> tap building -> Settings tab -> Business Type dropdown = Headquarters -> type name -> Save. Get BasicHr diploma. Phone/visit a Recruitment Agency contact -> dialog "candidate properties" input -> choose business + skill (HR Manager) + skill % + part/full-time + #candidates + deadline -> confirm, pay -> wait days for messages. (Alt: BizMan -> HQ -> Headhunters tab -> "+" plan -> assign a scheduled headhunter employee -> Start Recruiting with skill dropdown / target skill / deal-breakers.) Then Smartphone -> My Employees -> Candidates tab -> row for the manager -> (Negotiate optional) -> Hire button. My Employees -> that employee -> Assign-to-business dropdown -> the Headquarters. BizMan -> HQ -> Schedule tab -> drop the manager into work shifts.

SCREENSHOT-LEVEL FLOW — ASSIGN MANAGER + SET CONFIG (HR):
BizMan app -> BizManList -> Headquarters section -> tap the HQ (or its "HRManagers" counter). BizManBusiness opens on the HRManagers tab. Left pane = HrManagersPlanList: reorderable list of plan rows + a "+" row. Tap "+" -> AddPlan creates an empty HrManagerPlan. The new row is selected: it swaps its name label for a ManagerDropdown, and because assignedEmployeeId==null the HrManagerPlanUI detail pane is greyed with NoManagerAssignedPopUp showing an employee dropdown (only scheduled HR-skilled HQ employees). Pick one -> plan.AssignEmployee(id). Detail pane activates: set Training Target slider (0-100%), Replace Absent Employees toggle, negotiate/upgrade Health Insurance. Tap "assign employees" -> assignableEmployeesScrollerController lists unassigned employees; toggle each -> plan.assignedEmployees + employee.assignedHrManagerPlanId. "Fill" bulk-adds up to MaxEmployees; "Clear" removes all. Row now shows N/Max. For PRICING the plan config is a neighborhood dropdown + product price list; for LOGISTICS it is a warehouse dropdown + up to MaxDestinations destination stores each with per-product target amounts and +/- steppers (the direct template for the user's per-store limits + delivery targets).

modFeasibility: Nothing here is natively moddable. (1) Smartphone apps: sourced from a SmartphoneApps ScriptableObject asset + a hard 8-value AppName enum + name-matched prefab children of FullMenu.appsContainer. A new top-level app needs Harmony (patch FullMenu.Start/SelectApp) plus a prefab from an AssetBundle. (2) BizMan HQ tabs: BizManBusiness.SetUpTabs() is a hardcoded if/else, tab names are `const string` on BizMan, tab bodies are name-matched children of a `containers` transform with serialized component refs. Adding a "Store Manager" tab that looks native requires Harmony on SetUpTabs (inject the tab name) + SetTab (route it) + runtime-instantiating your own UGUI (or an AssetBundle prefab) under `containers`, reachable via InstanceBehavior<UIs>.Instance.fullMenu.bizMan.business. Reusing NoManagerAssignedPopUp / ReorderableList / BaTable cell views is possible only by reflection and is fragile. (3) Manager-as-employee: the typed subclass (HRManager:EmployeeInstance with WorkDaily override) is chosen only in RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate's switch and relies on save-system polymorphism; a modded subclass won't be spawned or serialized without Harmony on GenerateCandidate and the save serializer. (4) Plan persistence: plans live in fixed List<T> fields on GameInstance (hrManagerPlans, logisticsManagerPlans, ...). A mod cannot add a field to GameInstance, so a modded manager plan must persist in the mod's own JSON (as the current StoreManagerData file already does). RECOMMENDED MOD SHAPE that satisfies all 7 targets without new prefabs: keep the plan (supervised store addresses + per-store restock-budget cap + staffing level) in mod JSON; let the player designate the manager by picking an already-hired + HQ-assigned + scheduled employee (mirrors the vanilla dropdown filter assignedAddress==HQ && HasSkill && IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift) through a ModOptions panel or a Harmony-injected BizMan tab; run the daily logic on GlobalEvents.onNewDay, driving each supervised store's Entities.DeliveryContract (respecting DeliveryHelper.CanModifyContract); and surface every action with Notifications.Show + a permanent phone Contact + TextMessage, exactly the way LogisticsManagerPlan uses the "logistics_alerts" contact. The HR "manager plan" pattern (HrManagerPlan/HrManagerHelper) and the Logistics per-destination per-product target UI are the two structures to imitate.

Interaction/conflict between a modded store manager and vanilla systems that also touch the same stores: PricingManagerPlan (neighborhood price control), LogisticsManagerPlan (warehouse deliveries to the same store), HR 'replaceAbsentEmployees', and ScheduleAutoFiller/ScheduleAutoFillerUI.

Whether ba:skill_* skill tables (SkillHelper.AllSkillNames / SkillData) can be extended from a mod to introduce a real 'store manager' skill and wage curve, or whether the mod must repurpose an existing skill / no skill at all.
